title: Release-train phasing and blackout windows for multi-surface launches
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a coordinated phasing model and formal blackout/quiet windows that allow runtime, console, and API changes to ship with minimal cross-surface interference and clear rollback lanes. This ticket creates the canonical schedule template, gating criteria, and communication protocol for feature-group release trains across regions and capacity tiers.
background: We frequently see partial rollouts where a runtime change lands before console/SDK compatibility or an API schema change is not fully backfilled, causing client-side errors and paging. Current ad-hoc windows have reduced predictability for SRE and platform teams. This initiative standardizes phasing (canary -> regional ramp -> global) and prescribes blackout windows for non-essential changes during critical cutovers.
objectives: Create a phased release-train template mapping runtime/console/api artifacts to canonical stages (canary, regional ramp, global).
Define blackout / quiet windows for dependent subsystems and explicit exceptions process.
Establish gating checks (backfill completeness, e2e smoke, SDK compatibility) that must pass before progressing stages.
Produce a comms playbook and on-call escalation matrix for each stage and region.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable release-train template (PDF + Confluence doc) exists and is approved by SRE, Runtime, SDK, and Console leads.
Automatable gate checklist defined with measurable signals (smoke test pass rate, error budget, SDK usage telemetry) and owners for each gate.
Documented blackout windows and a formal exceptions flow that runs through PM + Eng triage and is logged to the launch calendar.
At least one upcoming launch uses the template end-to-end (postmortem captured).

risks: Overly conservative blackout windows could delay many launches and frustrate product teams.
Insufficient telemetry for gate automation — false positives could block healthy releases.
Cross-team alignment friction if ownership for a gate signal isn’t clear (e.g., who owns SDK compatibility).
Regional cloud outages during pilot could conflate template issues with infra instability.
decisions: Adopt three canonical phases: Canary (single-region), Regional Ramp (3-region stagger), Global.
Quiet periods will be enforced for non-critical changes during Canary->Regional cutover window; emergency fixes follow exceptions flow.
Use existing runtime smoke suite + SDK telemetry as primary gate signals; Console will add a lightweight UI smoke test.
Exceptions require sign-off from PM + ENG lead + SRE and must be recorded in the launch calendar with rationale.
